name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Product Ops should run a live, timestamped review queue where Legal stamps every repurposed asset before it goes public. This cuts the risk of brand or compliance slips in real time, not after the fact. The trade-off is slower repurposing speed, but that’s the price of avoiding costly rework or takedowns later.

name: Scriv
text: Legal’s stamp is a gate, not a fix. The real risk is Legal writing a static rulebook that Crumbles under edge cases—repurposing moves faster than rules can keep up. Better: Product Ops runs a live, timestamped review queue where Legal only flags *known* red lines up front, then lets the queue auto-clear assets unless a new red line is triggered. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with Legal only enforcing the top 5 recurring red lines—if repurposing speed drops less than 10%, the alternative wins.

name: Chisel
text:
Product Ops should run a live, timestamped review queue where Legal only pre-approves *known* red lines up front, then lets the queue auto-clear everything else. This keeps repurposing fast while stopping only the *certain* violations—edge cases get handled in real time, not by a rulebook that can’t keep up. The trade-off is Legal accepting that some gray-area assets will slip through until the queue flags them, but that’s better than slowing everything to a crawl with perfect but outdated rules.

name: Sift
text: The real risk is Legal pre-approving only “known” red lines while edge cases slip through—repurposing moves faster than Legal can catalog every violation, and the queue will auto-clear everything else. Instead, Product Ops should run a live, timestamped review queue where Legal *only* flags *known* red lines up front, then the queue auto-clears everything else—this keeps repurposing fast while stopping only the *certain* violations. The argument settles when Legal and Product Ops agree on a fixed list of red lines and the queue’s auto-clear threshold.

name: Scope
text: Product Ops runs a live, timestamped review queue where Legal stamps every repurposed asset before it goes public. This cuts the risk of brand or compliance slips in real time, not after the fact. The trade-off is slower repurposing speed, but that’s the price of avoiding costly rework or takedowns.

name: Scriv
text: Legal’s rubber stamp creates a bottleneck disguised as safety—repurposing stalls while Legal plays catch-up with every asset. Instead, Product Ops should run a live queue where Legal *only* blocks assets that violate *pre-approved, narrow* red lines (e.g., trademarks, regulated claims), letting the rest auto-clear. Settle it by testing: measure repurposing speed and error rates with the new queue for two weeks—if errors spike, widen the red lines; if speed drops, shrink them.

name: Reel
text: Product Ops runs a live, timestamped review queue where Legal only blocks assets that violate *pre-approved, narrow* red lines (e.g., trademarks, regulated claims), letting the rest auto-clear. This keeps repurposing fast while stopping only the *certain* violations—edge cases get handled in real time, not by a rulebook that can’t keep up. The trade-off is accepting a small, controlled risk of missed edge cases to avoid the bottleneck of Legal reviewing every asset.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: The real risk isn’t edge cases slipping through—it’s Legal’s *pre-approved red lines* becoming a static rulebook in disguise. Once Legal defines "narrow" violations, Product Ops will treat them as gospel, not as living constraints. The only way to settle this: Product Ops runs the queue, but Legal must *revisit* the red lines every 30 days with real repurposing data—no rubber stamps, no frozen rules.
